whyThisFileExists: A constant spelled in a register entry, six skills and an agent is eight copies, and the stale one is the one a reader finds. CLAUDE.md § Three kinds of file, and never a fourth puts every constant a tool or a prompt reads in a policy file under a key, with its reason beside it. `docs/decisions.md` § D-02 held the label's spelling only until this file existed; § D-03 moved it here.

specChangeLabelMeans: The tracker label on a product change's epic and on every one of its tasks (docs/decisions.md § D-02, item 3). change-propose puts it on the epic and the children inherit it; the general sweeps of the queue exclude it (`bd ready --exclude-label` in the bead skill and the fan-out-work agent), and change-plan, change-build, change-verify and change-finalize find the epic by it. Changing it here strands every open change: relabel their epics and tasks in the same change, and respell the label in every skill and agent that cites this key, which `npm run openspec:check` names. Decided 2026-09-23 with D-02; moved here 2026-09-23 by D-03.
specIdPrefixesMeans: The prefix every scenario and NFR ID of a capability carries: each key a capability (a directory under openspec/specs/, or under a change's specs/), each value its prefix. The ID rules, what `npm run openspec:check` refuses and where the next free ID comes from are the header of scripts/check-openspec.mjs, their one home under docs/decisions.md § D-13. A change that adds a capability adds its key here in the same change; renaming a prefix re-keys every header and every test that names it. Where it loses: a reader who meets `[CLS-014]` in a test name looks the prefix up here to learn its capability, where the full capability name would have said so. Decided 2026-09-28 with D-13, the prefixes chosen by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-j09.3).
testTraceHashLengthMeans: How many characters of an artifact's lowercase hex sha256 a test's `// trace:` line carries as the version of that artifact it was written against: a scenario's block with its requirement's statement, an NFR requirement's block, a Binding Surface or a contract file (the header of scripts/test-trace.mjs, the convention's one home under docs/decisions.md § D-13, item 17). A hash is compared only with the current hash of the same block, so it is a version stamp and not an identity: 12 characters leave one edit in 2^48 unnoticed, where all 64 would make a trace line 52 characters longer for each artifact it cites. Changing it makes every hash in every test the wrong length, which `npm run calculator:test` then refuses: rewrite them from `node scripts/test-trace.mjs cite` in the same change. Where it loses: an edit whose block hashes to the same 12 characters leaves its tests current, where the full 64 would not. Decided 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.5).
testTraceLayersMeans: The layers a test may declare in its `// trace:` metadata, each key a layer and each value its default orchestration level, as docs/test-strategy.md § Environment orchestration rules gives them; `null` where the level is declared per test, as it is for a fitness function. A test at a level above its layer's default records why, and a test at or below it records no reason; scripts/test-trace.mjs, whose header is the convention's one home, refuses either slip and a layer this key does not list. Mutation is not a layer: a mutation run references the suite it targets (docs/test-strategy.md § Traceability, rule 7). Levels 2 and 3 are not adopted until a product needs them (docs/decisions.md § D-13, item 17), so an integration test here runs at level 1, below its default, and records nothing. The layer of each of the calculator's test files was the maintainer's choice (asdlc-openspec-j09.5's notes). Adding a layer here lets a test declare it; removing one strands every test that declares it, which `npm run calculator:test` then refuses. Where it loses: a default changed here moves the level of every test that states none, without a line of any test changing. Decided 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.5).
testInventoryTrailerMeans: The key of the git trailer that records an architect's decision to remove, skip or weaken a test on a branch (docs/test-strategy.md § Test ownership). `npm run tests:inventory:check` (scripts/check-test-inventory.mjs, whose header is the rule's one home under docs/decisions.md § D-13, item 17) compares a branch's tests with its merge base with `origin/main`, and refuses each test removed, given a skip, todo or only, or left with fewer assertions, unless a commit on the branch carries `<this key>: <remove|skip|weaken> <file> "<test name>" <reason>` in the last paragraph of its message, where git reads trailers, with this key spelled exactly, case included; that header holds the grammar. The key names the role the strategy gives the decision, the architect, who is the build workflow's triage together with the session running change-build (D-13, item 16). Changing it leaves every trailer written under the old spelling on an open branch unread, so the gate refuses what it cleared; a trailer already on the trunk is never read again, since the gate reads only a branch's own commits. Where it loses: any commit's author can write the trailer, so it records that a decision was made and why, not who made it; the pull-request reviewer and the person merging read it. Decided 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.9).
traceObligationLayersMeans: The layers whose tests count toward a scenario's obligation of at least one happy-path test and one negative test: docs/test-strategy.md § Scenario coverage counts functional, integration, contract and E2E tests, and not unit tests. Each is a key of `testTraceLayers`. `npm run trace:check` refuses a scenario with no happy-path or no negative test at one of these layers, unless the ratchet baseline lists that obligation or the scenario's happy-path test declares its negative not applicable, and refuses a layer here that `testTraceLayers` does not list (the header of tools/trace/trace.ts). Fitness is not here: a fitness function proves an NFR, whose scenarios owe neither test (docs/decisions.md § D-13, item 14). Where it loses: a scenario proved only by a thorough unit test counts as unproved until a functional test repeats it. Adding `unit` lets a unit test meet the obligation, which the strategy refuses. Taken from the strategy's text, which D-13 adopted, on 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.7).
thresholdPercentsMeans: The thresholds `npm run thresholds:check` and `npm run thresholds:commands:check` hold the code a branch changes under apps/ to, each a whole percentage: `lines`, of its changed code lines, those Node's own coverage counts run; `branches`, of the branches Node reports on those lines, those taken; `mutation`, of the mutants StrykerJS makes over the changed code of the Routines and, in a run of their own, of the Commands, those detected. What each counts, who counts it and the value that would mean the project is not viable are count-index.md § Rates and metrics. docs/test-strategy.md § Thresholds gives them as supplied, at least 80% on changed Commands and Routines and at least 90% line and branch coverage, and docs/decisions.md § D-13, items 8 and 9, measures them over the lines a branch changes against origin/main. Each is judged only over its minimum sample, `thresholdMinSamples`. Raising one refuses a change the gate passed before; lowering one passes weaker tests. Where it loses: a change whose every line is run and every mutant detected by tests that each check one thing passes at 100%, and only the honesty lens, reading the tests, sees how little they check. The calculator's first measurement is in the header of scripts/check-thresholds.mjs. Decided 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.10), from the strategy D-13 adopted.
thresholdMinSamplesMeans: The sample below which `scripts/check-thresholds.mjs` gives no rate: `lines`, changed code lines; `branches`, changed branches; `mutants`, the mutants of changed code one mutation run makes, leaving out one a comment ignores and one whose test run errored. Below it the gate prints the counts and refuses each one uncovered, untaken or undetected that no directive excuses with a reason (count-index.md § Rates and metrics; docs/decisions.md § D-13, item 9). They are choices, not measurements: the calculator's past changes measured by the spike asdlc-openspec-j09.2 were either comment-only or at least 50 mutants, 35 code lines and 16 branches, so its data cannot place a floor between. At 20 mutants one is 5 points and 80% tolerates 4 undetected, where the largest net change the spike saw between two runs was 3; at 20 code lines 90% tolerates 2 missed; at 10 branches one is 10 points and 90% tolerates 1. The maintainer chose them on 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.2's notes, answer 4). Raising one sends more changes to the count rule, which refuses any single gap; lowering one lets a rate over a handful pass or fail on one line. Where it loses: a change with 15 mutants and 3 undetected fails, where as a rate it would pass at exactly 80%. Decided 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.10).
thresholdScopeMeans: What `scripts/check-thresholds.mjs` counts as the product's code: `code`, the globs of the files whose lines and mutants it measures, and `tests`, the globs of the files it leaves out, every test file and any helper beside one; a file both match is a test's. Each is a glob under apps/, relative to the repository's root, and they are also Node's coverage include and exclude globs. Only JavaScript is listed, since V8 records the coverage of JavaScript and StrykerJS mutates it here; an app's HTML and CSS are not measured. What counts as changed is the header's: the lines `git diff -U0` gives against the merge base with origin/main, and a file git does not track yet, whole (docs/decisions.md § D-13, item 8). Only changed source lines are mutated, so a change to a file `tests` matches mutates nothing: the maintainer's choice of 2026-09-29 (asdlc-openspec-j09.10's notes), which leaves a weakened test to the test-inventory gate (asdlc-openspec-j09.9). Adding an extension brings its files into both metrics; widening `tests` takes files out of both. Where it loses: a test helper kept outside an app's test/ directory is measured as the product's code, and a script inline in an HTML page is not measured at all. Decided 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.10).
mutationCommandsMeans: The Commands: each key a file under apps/ whose code the tests reach by spawning a process, each value the test files its mutation run runs. `npm run thresholds:commands:check` mutates a Command with StrykerJS's command runner, one mutant at a time, which sees what a spawned process runs. Every other file `thresholdScope` counts as code is a Routine, which `npm run thresholds:check` mutates with the tap runner over every test file no Command lists, so no test that spawns a server is run by the tap runner, which leaves such a server running when it ends a failing test's process (the header of scripts/check-thresholds.mjs has the measurements). A Command's run is a CI step and a change-verify run and not a pre-push job, for its cost, 181-186 s wall for all 72 of serve.js's mutants, a change to every line of it, on the host that header names: the maintainer's choice of 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.2's notes, answer 3), an exception to the gate ladder that docs/decisions.md § D-04 records in its amendment of 2026-09-29. Adding a Command moves its mutants from pre-push to CI; a spawned file left out is scored by the tap runner, which cannot see what the spawned process runs, as 25 of serve.js's 72 mutants were not seen. Where it loses: serve.js's exported functions, which its tests also call in-process, wait for CI with the rest of the file. Decided 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.10).

assetLabelsMeans: What an issue a run files `discovered-from` would fix: one label for each kind of file it would change, each key the label and each value what it covers (CLAUDE.md § The task store says when). Paired with its `foundAtLabels` label it is the recurrence signal the retired learning loop was to derive (docs/decisions.md § D-06): `bd count -l <a found-at label> --by-label` counts the pairs. An issue that fits none of these gets the label it needs added here first, with its date, in the change that files it. Renaming a label strands every issue that carries it: relabel them in the same change. Decided 2026-09-24 with D-06 (asdlc-openspec-6dn); the eight values were fitted to the issues discovered from asdlc-openspec-zgh.

foundAtLabels.found:bead: while an issue was worked through the bead skill, or a lane of the fan-out-work agent
foundAtLabels.found:review: by looking back at a run after it ended: a prompt review, or a person or session reviewing a finished change

foundAtLabelsMeans: Where an issue a run files `discovered-from` was found: exactly one label, the stage that was running, each key the label and each value when it applies (CLAUDE.md § The task store says when). `found:review` is the count of what got through every stage and was caught only looking back. An issue filed before D-06 carries one only where its own text says which stage found it. Decided 2026-09-24 with D-06 (asdlc-openspec-6dn), after a second opinion on the retirement pointed out that the loop's recurrence signal is the pair of where a correction was found and what it would fix.

rerouteLabels.reroute:build: change-verify or change-finalize sent work back to change-build: a gap in the code, a finding the user made a new task, or a test trace:check refused after the archive
rerouteLabels.reroute:design: a later stage revised the design
rerouteLabels.reroute:plan: a later stage added a task to the epic
rerouteLabels.reroute:propose: a later stage revised the proposal or a delta spec

rerouteLabelsMeans: Labels on a product change's epic, one for each earlier stage a later stage sent the change back to, each key the label and each value when it applies (CLAUDE.md § Product work runs as OpenSpec-format changes says when). A label is a set: it records that the change went back, not how often. `bd count -t epic -l <specChangeLabel> --by-label` then answers how many changes needed their spec, design or plan reworked after the stage that wrote it, the rework a label on a found issue never sees because it lands as commits inside the change. Decided 2026-09-24 with D-06 (asdlc-openspec-6dn), after the same second opinion showed that the calculator change's largest corrections, its spec revised during build and its design amended at verify, became no issue.
buildReviewLensesMeans: The reviewers `.claude/workflows/build-change-task.js` runs on one task of a product change, chosen by what the task mainly changes: each key an `assetLabels` key, each value the lens keys, one reviewer each. The parent session picks the key (`.claude/skills/change-build/SKILL.md` § 3. Build it, and prove it). The lens prompts are the workflow's own, and a task adds only its focus to them, so no run reviews through more lenses than its set. `asset:spec` has no set: a task never edits its own delta specs, and a spec revision is the parent's, under that skill's § 5. A documentation, register or prompt task runs at most two lenses: the register-and-briefing task asdlc-openspec-zgh.6 ran three and spent 35 agents and 2,946,105 tokens to confirm 2 of the 9 findings it sent to skeptics, both minor (wf_f256bc20-ffb, a workflow state file outside this repository). A new key must be an `assetLabels` key, and a lens must exist in the workflow's library before a set names it; npm run workflows:selftest runs a clean control for every key and refuses a lens the workflow does not have. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-d6b).
buildReviewSkepticsMeans: How many skeptics the workflow sends to confirm one finding of each severity. Each judges the finding against the delta specs, the design and the task, and answers upheld, refuted or unverified; a majority of those sent decides, and a finding with no majority goes back to the parent as unverified, never as refuted (the workflow's header holds the mechanics). A spec contradiction is always confirmed at `blocker`, because a confirmed one halts the run. The calculator change (asdlc-openspec-zgh) sent every finding to three: 58 findings went to 174 skeptics and 19 were upheld, and all 16 that its build runs confirmed were minor (the session's wf_*.json workflow state files, outside this repository; the figures are re-derived in a note on asdlc-openspec-d6b). Lowering `blocker` below 3 lets one vote halt the run on a spec contradiction. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-d6b). `major` lowered from 3 to 1 on 2026-09-28 by D-16 (asdlc-openspec-hsg), item 3, which the maintainer chose over the recommendation to leave this key for asdlc-openspec-j09.11 to resize with the pilot's figures; `blocker` and `minor` stay. Where it loses: one vote now decides whether a major finding is confirmed, fixed and earns another round, where a majority of three would outvote a skeptic that misreads it.
buildReviewMaxRoundsMeans: The most review rounds one run of the workflow makes. A round reviews, confirms and fixes, and the next reviews that fix; after the last round's fix the run stops and reports the fix as unreviewed, and the parent reads its diff. In the calculator change no round after the second confirmed anything: its two third rounds sent 2 findings to skeptics and confirmed none (wf_ad92e5b6-d54 and wf_2d38608d-3a8, workflow state files outside this repository). Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-d6b).
buildReviewMajorSeveritiesMeans: The severities of a confirmed defect that earn another review round. A round that confirms none of these is the last: its confirmed minor defects are fixed and the run stops, so review does not loop on small findings, as `.claude/skills/change-build/SKILL.md` § 5. What the build turns up keeps it from looping on coverage. No build run of the calculator change confirmed a finding above minor, yet five of them ran a second round and two a third (the session's wf_*.json workflow state files, outside this repository). Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-d6b).
buildRedFirstKindsMeans: The kinds of task, each an `assetLabels` key, held to the red run: `.claude/workflows/build-change-task.js` asks every builder to see each scenario the task names fail before it changes the code under test, and stops a run of a kind listed here as `not-red`, before any review, when the builder returns neither a red record nor an already-green report for one of them (its header holds the mechanics; `docs/decisions.md` § D-14). A task of a kind not listed, a docs, prompt, register, environment, tool or gate task today, is asked for the same records and not held to them. Decided 2026-09-28 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-fye): `asset:product`, `asset:tool` and `asset:gate`, the kinds whose proofs are commands, were proposed, and the maintainer chose `asset:product` alone. Where that loses: a gate's new selftest case that passes before the refusal it holds exists is not caught by a red run, only later by the honesty lens. Adding `asset:tool` loses where a tool task only renames a flag: it has no proof that can fail first, so its builder reports it already green and the parent judges it. npm run workflows:selftest stops as `not-red` a task of each kind listed here whose builder returns neither record for a named scenario, runs such a task of each kind not listed on to review, and refuses a kind that is not an `assetLabels` key.
buildIndependentKindsMeans: The kinds of task, each an `assetLabels` key, for which `.claude/workflows/build-change-task.js` runs the test-builder beside the builder and then the architect's runs of its tests (the workflow's header holds the mechanics; `docs/test-strategy.md` § Build Agents; `docs/decisions.md` § D-13, items 16 and 17). A task of a kind listed here must name its app (`args.app`). A kind not listed is built and reviewed as before, with no independent test. `asset:product` alone, since the product's code under `apps/` is what a Binding Surface and a contract describe. Where it loses: an `asset:tool` task that changes a script an app's tests run through gets no independent test. npm run workflows:selftest runs a task of this kind through the test-builder and the architect, and refuses a kind that is not an `assetLabels` key. Decided 2026-09-28 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-j09.11).
buildArchitectMaxRoundsMeans: The most runs of the test-builder's tests one run of the workflow makes. Each run triages every failing file into one route and, but for the last, acts on the routes: one fixer for the fix-app routes, and the test-builder again for the rewrite-test ones; the last run's failures are triaged and returned, and stop the run as `architect-failing`. So 2 is one fix or rewrite and a second run to see it hold. It is a choice, not a measurement: no change has yet run the architect's triage. Where it loses: a failure whose fix needs a second attempt stops the run for the parent, where 3 would have tried again. npm run workflows:selftest stops a run whose tests fail at every run as `architect-failing` after this many. Decided 2026-09-28 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-j09.11).
independentInputsMeans: Everything the test-builder may read, as paths under the change's worktree, `{change}` and `{app}` filled in from the workflow's arguments: the proposal, the design, the delta specs, the app's Binding Surface, its contract artifacts and fitness records, its own earlier tests, and the header of scripts/test-trace.mjs, the home of the convention its tests follow. A path names a file or every file under a directory. A script is given as its header alone, its first block comment, since a header is where a rule lives and the code below it is not the test-builder's to read. The epic's children come from the tracker beside them, without their notes (`docs/test-strategy.md` § Shared inputs). The test-builder has no tool, so what is not given here it never sees; the workflow drops any path Setup returns outside these and logs it. Adding a path lets the test-builder see what the app-builder may have written: never add a path under `apps/` outside these. Where it loses: a living spec the change leaves alone is not given, so a test of a MODIFIED scenario sees only its new text. npm run workflows:selftest drops a planted path outside these from the test-builder's prompt. Decided 2026-09-28 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-j09.11).
independentTestDirMeans: Where the test-builder's tests live, `{app}` filled in: below it a directory per stage, `build` for a test at a layer of `architectRunLayers` that runs at build and `verify` for every other, then one per layer of `independentLayers`, each test a `<name>.test.js`. Ownership is this path prefix: the workflow stops as `not-independent` a builder or fixer whose changed files enter it for any app, and a test-builder file outside it or under the wrong stage. `npm run calculator:test` does not reach it, since its pattern is not recursive; `npm run calculator:test:independent` runs its `build` stage at each push and in CI, and `npm run calculator:test:verify` its `verify` stage, which change-verify's fresh run, scripts/fresh-run.mjs, runs at Verify (asdlc-openspec-j09.14), so no E2E test or Verify-deferred fitness function runs at a push (`docs/test-strategy.md` § Build exit criteria). Moving it strands every test under the old path until they move with it. Where it loses: an app-builder's own consumer-side contract test lives outside it, so a count of contract tests by directory undercounts, where a count by the tests' metadata would not. Decided 2026-09-28 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-j09.11).
independentLayersMeans: The layers the test-builder writes, each a `testTraceLayers` key and a directory under `independentTestDir`, as `docs/test-strategy.md` § Test ownership gives them to it; every other layer is the app-builder's, and an architect may ask the app-builder for a lower-layer test only at one of those. Adding a layer here gives it to the test-builder and takes it from the app-builder. Decided 2026-09-28 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-j09.11).
architectRunLayersMeans: The layers of `independentLayers` whose tests the workflow's architect runs against the build after the review, as `docs/test-strategy.md` § Test ownership has it: contract tests and the fitness functions whose execution environment is `build`. An E2E test is written and returned, and runs at Verify. Adding `e2e` runs every journey after every task, which the strategy leaves to the verifier. Decided 2026-09-28 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-j09.11).
verifyTraceMaxScenariosMeans: The most scenarios one tracer of `.claude/workflows/verify-change-trace.js` traces. The change-verify session groups a change's scenarios, whole requirements of one capability where they fit, into groups of at most this many, and the workflow runs one tracer per group and refuses a larger group. A tracer reads every proof of its group line by line and runs each, so a larger group is fewer agents and a longer read for each; a change with 61 scenarios, as the calculator change had, needs at least 6 tracers. The maintainer chose it on 2026-09-28 from a recommendation put with the case where it loses, recorded in the notes of asdlc-openspec-as9. Decided 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-as9).
verifyTraceDesignLensesMeans: How many design lenses the workflow runs on a change that has a design.md: the session splits the design's decisions into this many parts, and one agent holds the code to each. A change with no design.md runs none. On a run again after a fix or a rebase, only a lens whose part the diff changes runs again and the others keep their reading, as "Running again" in `.claude/skills/change-verify/SKILL.md` § 4. Every scenario is traced says; the workflow refuses a first run with another number, and a run again whose lenses and kept readings do not add up to it. The calculator change's verify ran 3 (asdlc-openspec-as9). Decided 2026-09-28 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-as9).
verifyTraceSkepticsMeans: How many skeptics the workflow sends to judge each gap, whether a tracer's row shows it or a design lens reports it, but for a proof that failed or did not pass when run, which no vote clears. Each answers upheld, refuted or unverified; a majority of those sent decides, and a gap with no majority goes back to the session as unverified, never as refuted (the workflow's header holds the mechanics). Every gap blocks the change, so there is no severity to size by, and one count serves. Where it loses: a change with 61 scenarios and 4 gaps runs about 6 tracers, 3 lenses and 12 skeptics, 21 agents, where one skeptic for each gap would run 8 fewer, though a single vote would then decide whether a gap blocks the change (the maintainer's choice of 2026-09-28, in the notes of asdlc-openspec-as9). Decided 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-as9).
worktreeGcMinAgeHoursMeans: On a host where `scripts/prune-worktree-branches.mjs` (`npm run worktree:gc`, also run by the `WorktreeRemove` hook) has no liveness check, neither `/proc` nor `lsof`, the hours HEAD must have sat still in a clean worktree whose branch is contained in the trunk before the sweep removes it; the script's header says how HEAD's last move is read. Where a liveness check works it is not read. It is 24 because a lane's run is measured in hours and a freshly cut worktree is clean and contained from its first second, so anything shorter can remove a live lane (asdlc-openspec-zlz). Raising it keeps an abandoned checkout, and its branch, on disk longer; lowering it lets the sweep remove a lane that has not yet committed. Where it loses: a session that works more than 24 hours in one worktree without a commit, checkout or rebase is removed under it on such a host, where a longer threshold would have kept it. Decided 2026-09-29 (asdlc-openspec-zlz).
worktreeGcMergedPrLimitMeans: How many of the trunk branch's merged pull requests, newest first, `scripts/prune-worktree-branches.mjs` asks `gh pr list` for, once per sweep, to prove a branch contained when its tip is one's head: a rebase merge gives the trunk new SHAs, and a neighbouring line changed on the trunk gives the replayed commits new patch-ids, so GitHub's record is the one proof that survives both (asdlc-openspec-dxf). The repository had 72 merged pull requests when this was set; 500 lists them all for a while yet, in one call that took 0.71 s. Raising it lengthens the call; lowering it leaves a branch whose pull request is older than the last one listed to the patch-id proofs. Where it loses: past 500 merged pull requests, a branch merged before the newest 500 whose patches changed as they landed is kept, where a larger limit would have proved it. Decided 2026-09-29 (asdlc-openspec-dxf).
worktreeGcGhTimeoutSecondsMeans: The most seconds `scripts/prune-worktree-branches.mjs` waits for its one `gh pr list` call before it reads no merged pull requests and falls through to the patch-id proofs. The `WorktreeRemove` hook runs the sweep synchronously on every teardown, so a host with no network, where a connection can hang rather than fail, would otherwise stall each teardown for as long as `gh` waits. The call took 0.71 s online on 2026-09-29. Raising it lets a slow network still answer, at that cost to an offline teardown; lowering it drops the proof on a slow one. Where it loses: on a network slower than 10 s, a branch whose patches changed as they landed is kept, where a longer wait would have proved it. Decided 2026-09-29 (asdlc-openspec-dxf).
freshRunDeadlineSecondsMeans: The most seconds one call of `scripts/fresh-run.mjs` may take, its fresh run or a `--rerun`, from setting its deadline to its last child: a child still running when it passes is killed with every process it started, the clone is removed and the run is refused, saying so. It sits below 600 s, the longest a session's Bash call may wait, so a call the session gives that timeout (the script's header names it) ends by this deadline and its cleanup rather than by the harness killing it with the clone left behind. The Commands' mutation run took 181-186 s over every line of serve.js (the header of scripts/check-thresholds.mjs), inside it with room for the install and the tests. Raising it past 600 s lets the harness kill a call before its own cleanup runs; lowering it refuses a run whose Commands' mutants take longer. Where it loses: a change that touches many Commands at once can take longer than this, and is refused where a longer deadline would have measured it. Decided 2026-09-29 (asdlc-openspec-j09.14, from its pre-PR review).
graphifyVersionMeans: The graphify release `scripts/code-graph.mjs` (`npm run code-graph`) requires: `graphify --version` must print it before the script builds, and the script's install line is `uv tool install "graphifyy[mcp]==<this>"`. It is pinned because the script relies on that release's behaviour, read from its source on 2026-10-01: the `claude-cli` backend and `GRAPHIFY_CLAUDE_CLI_MODEL`, the text of its partial-extraction warnings, and the file types in `graphifySemanticExtensions`. Moving it means checking those against the new release and the script's header first. Moving it without that check can let a reworded warning or a new file type through unseen; never moving it leaves everyone on an old release. Where it loses: a graphify fix, such as one to the `graphify update` erosion `docs/decisions.md` § D-20 records, reaches nobody here until someone moves this. Decided 2026-10-01 (asdlc-openspec-rsc).
graphifyClaudeCliModelMeans: The model graphify's `claude-cli` backend extracts the documents with when `scripts/code-graph.mjs` builds. The script passes it as `GRAPHIFY_CLAUDE_CLI_MODEL`, the one setting that backend reads for extraction, and `claude -p --model` takes an alias or a full model name. The script also passes it to `graphify cluster-only` as `--model`, so the communities are named with the same model. It is `opus` because the graph the maintainer judged worth having, with its links between documents and code, came from Opus agents, and nothing has measured what a smaller model would miss. Lowering it to `sonnet` or `haiku` spends less of each person's plan per document. Where it loses: a first build sends every document, so each engineer's first build spends Opus on all of them, where a smaller model would cost less. What the script's first build costs is not yet measured (asdlc-openspec-3rx); the agent skill's first build, on the same documents with Opus, cost $10.40 at Langfuse's prices (`docs/decisions.md` § D-20). Decided 2026-10-01 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-rsc).
graphifyOutDirMeans: The folder under the primary checkout that `scripts/code-graph.mjs` builds the local code graph into. The script passes it to graphify as `GRAPHIFY_OUT`. `.gitignore` ignores it, unanchored, and the `code-graph` skill, the READMEs, `docs/decisions.md` § D-20 and the script's header spell it; no gate holds them to this value, so a rename edits each of them in the same change, D-20 by an amendment. It is graphify's own default, so a person running graphify by hand finds the same folder. Where it loses: a rename that misses `.gitignore` would let a person commit the graph, which `docs/decisions.md` § D-20 rules out. Decided 2026-10-01 (asdlc-openspec-rsc).
graphifyMcpServerNameMeans: The name `scripts/code-graph.mjs` registers graphify's MCP server under at Claude Code's local scope, which makes its tools `mcp__<this>__<tool>`. The `code-graph` skill, the worktree briefing's carve-out, the READMEs and `docs/decisions.md` § D-20 spell it; no gate holds them to this value, so a rename edits each of them in the same change, D-20 by an amendment, and each person runs `npm run code-graph:mcp` again. Where it loses: a person who already registered another server under this name at local scope has it replaced. Decided 2026-10-01 (asdlc-openspec-rsc).
graphifySemanticExtensionsMeans: The file extensions whose graph items `scripts/code-graph.mjs` stamps `_origin: "semantic"` after each build that changed the graph, with the items of the node types graphify's parser never makes and every edge that touches one. They are graphify 0.9.73's document, paper, image and office types (lines 48 to 51 of its `detect.py`), every type it sends to the LLM rather than parsing. The stamp stops `graphify update`, if anyone runs it, from deleting those items as parser output (the script's header). Re-derive the list from that file whenever `graphifyVersion` moves. Adding an extension graphify parses as code would mark parser output as semantic, which `update` then never refreshes; leaving one out lets `update` erode that type's items. Where it loses: a type graphify adds in a later release goes unstamped until this list is re-derived. Decided 2026-10-01 (asdlc-openspec-rsc).
typesafeModelMeans: The model every TypeSafe question in this repository is sent to, read through `tools/lib/typesafe.ts` by each tool that asks one. Pinned and not `jev-latest`, so a run can be reproduced and a probability means the same on the day it is read as on the day its threshold was set: a threshold is calibrated to one model, and the 2026-09-29 experiments behind the first caller (`asdlc-openspec-6yt`) ran on this one. It is changed here only, by a person who has re-measured every caller's threshold on the new model. Where it loses: the service retires a pinned model one day, and every caller then fails with the SDK's error until this key is edited, where `jev-latest` would have gone on answering with a model no threshold was measured on.
citationSupportMinProbabilityMeans: The probability of `supports` under which `npm run citations:support` prints a citation as not supported: the citation is read against this, and a citation at or above it is silent. Measured over the 437 citations the command judged in this repository on 2026-09-30, before this change's own files were added to it, with `jev-1.13.0` (the `--min` flag re-runs it): 68 fell under 0.5, 21 under 0.3 and 3 under 0.1, and a re-run moved the count at 0.5 by a few (65 to 68). It is 0.3 because a list of 68 is not one a person reads to the end, where 21 include the one defect a reading confirmed, `docs/playbook.md:53` citing `README.md` § Setup for a sentence that sits in the file table at README.md:93, under 0.15 in both runs. The note on `asdlc-openspec-6yt.2` proposed 0.5 with 2 of 120 real citations flagged there; that figure did not reproduce over the whole repository, and the count here is the one this key is set from. Raising it toward 1 prints more citations and more noise; lowering it toward 0 prints only the surest ones and misses a borderline pointer. Where it loses: a sentence that points at a section for where a step lives and not for what it says (`Decided by: <file> § 3`) scores low however well cited, and most of the 21 are of that shape.
citationSupportSkipPathsMeans: Files, or path prefixes, whose citations `npm run citations:support` does not judge, so a person is not sent to read what cannot be edited. The register is the one: an entry is never rewritten, a later decision adds a dated amendment (`CLAUDE.md` § Decisions live in the register), so an entry that cites what a document said before an amendment is correct history and reads as contradicted to a judge given the document as it is now. It is a file's path, exactly or as a prefix, and the files under a `HISTORY` root in `tools/citations/scan.ts` are skipped without being listed here. Where it loses: a citation written wrongly in the register goes unjudged; `citations:check` still checks that it resolves.
citationSupportSectionMaxCharsMeans: The most characters of a cited passage `npm run citations:support` sends TypeSafe with a citation: a section whole up to it, and a cut, marked in the report, beyond. Set at the 32,000 that the note on `asdlc-openspec-6yt.2` gives as the state budget; the SDK and API pages read for that task state no limit, and a request the service refused would fail the run and not be skipped. The section is sent whole because the 2026-09-29 experiment's fixed passage carried up to 6,000 characters and separated real citations from swapped ones at an AUC of 0.959, and a claim about the rest of a section cannot be judged from its start. Raising it costs input tokens on every long section; lowering it cuts a passage before the sentence a citation is about. Where it loses: a section of a prompt file with no headings after its label runs to the end of the file, and is cut where the sentence cited may lie past the cut.
citationSupportClaimLineMaxCharsMeans: The most characters of each of the three lines round a pointer that `npm run citations:support` sends as the claim: a longer line is cut to a window of this width round the pointer, so the pointer is never cut off. It exists for the table row and the JSON string that hold a whole paragraph on one line: on 2026-09-30 this file had 41 lines over 800 characters, the longest 7,476, and a pointer on such a line would otherwise send it whole as a claim and dwarf the sentence about the pointer. 800 is the width the first version used; it was not measured against a range of widths. The three-line claim itself was measured against the pointer line alone (see `citationSupportMinProbabilityMeans`). Raising it sends more of a long row, and more of the neighbours a pointer's sentence does not concern; lowering it cuts a long sentence's own words away from its pointer. Where it loses: a table row holding several pointers is windowed round the first one named on it, so the other pointers on that row are judged against text that may not carry their own sentence.
citationSupportLineContextMeans: How many lines either side of a cited line or range `npm run citations:support` sends as the passage for a `file.md:NN` citation, which names a line and not a section. Three carries the sentence a line belongs to in this repository's wrapped prose without taking in a neighbouring section. Raising it takes in the next paragraph and the judge can then be satisfied by a passage the citation did not point at; lowering it to none judges one wrapped fragment of a sentence. Where it loses: a table row cited by line is judged against its neighbouring rows, which can support a claim about the row above it.
citationSupportConcurrencyMeans: How many TypeSafe requests `npm run citations:support` has in flight at once. Sixteen is enough to judge the whole repository in seconds, and the bound keeps a rate limit (the SDK retries a 429) from being met at five hundred requests at once, which the 2026-09-29 experiment's unbounded fan-out never tested. Raising it shortens a whole-repository run and raises the chance of a 429; lowering it to 1 sends one at a time. Where it loses: nothing but wall time, since a failed call fails the run at any width.
citationSupportMaxCitationsMeans: The most citations one run of `npm run citations:support` will send TypeSafe: over it the run refuses, and says to narrow it with `--file` or to raise this key, so a runaway walk, such as a scanner that began reading a generated file, cannot spend without limit. Set at about three times the 437 the whole repository held on 2026-09-30 before this change's own files were added (`npm run citations:support -- --dry-run` counts it now), so ordinary growth never trips it. A run with no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` sends nothing, judges offline by word overlap (`citationSupportOverlapMinShare`) and is not held to it. Raising it is a person's edit; lowering it below that count refuses every whole-repository run. Where it loses: a repository that grows past it refuses the whole-repository run until the key is raised, and `--file` still works.
citationSupportOverlapMinShareMeans: The offline fallback's threshold: when `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is not set, `npm run citations:support` weighs each word by how few of the scanned files hold it, leaves out the pointer's own words and its section's heading, and prints a citation whose cited passage holds less than this share of its claim's weight; a share at or above it is silent. The maintainer chose this fallback on 2026-09-30 (`asdlc-openspec-6yt.6`) over Claude Code headless and the Anthropic API, knowing the loss below. Measured that day over the 442 citations the command judges, against one TypeSafe run on `jev-1.13.0` that put 27 under `citationSupportMinProbability` (0.3): the share ranks those 27 below the rest at an AUC of 0.69; at 0.05 it prints 8, 2 of them among the 27; at 0.1, 26 and 5; at 0.15, 57 and 10; at 0.2, 85 and 11; at 0.3, 156 and 15. It is 0.1 because that prints a list about as long as the TypeSafe one, which a person reads to the end. Raising it prints more citations, most of them sound; lowering it prints only the claims that share almost nothing with their section. Where it loses: `docs/playbook.md:53`, the one defect a reading confirmed among TypeSafe's list, cites `README.md` § Setup for a sentence that sits in that file's table, and its claim shares 0.33 of its weight with § Setup, so only a setting above 0.33 shows it, where 0.3 already prints 156. A claim that contradicts its section shares its words and is silent, and a claim that paraphrases its section is printed; the `--min` flag re-runs it at another share.
promptReviewAnalysisMarkerMeans: The word that opens the first line of a run's analysis, a note on the issue or epic the run worked, followed by a space and the run id (`.claude/skills/close-prompt-run/SKILL.md` § 1. Write the analysis, or none, says how both are written). `bd list --all --notes-contains` finds every analysis by it, so it must appear in no other note: changing it strands every analysis written under the old word, which no review then finds, so a change rewrites them or reviews them first. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-08 (asdlc-openspec-lzr).
promptReviewReadMarkerMeans: The word that opens the line a review appends to an issue for each analysis on it that the review read, followed by a space, the run id, a space, and the review's pull request or `no change`. It covers a slow week, when `promptReviewDueCount` analyses take longer to gather. Nothing checks it but the closing step of a run, so in a week when no prompt runs an analysis waits past it for the next run of any prompt; the maintainer chose that over a scheduler (D-08). It is a choice, not a measurement. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-08 (asdlc-openspec-lzr).
promptReviewHeldMarkerMeans: The word that opens a held line, which a review appends to the issue carrying a run's analysis for each finding that run showed and the review did not carry into its pull request: below the threshold, set aside by its file's agent, or on a branch the skeptics did not uphold (`.claude/agents/continuous-prompt-improvement.md` § 6. Mark what was read says how the line is written). The next review counts a finding from these lines, so changing the word strands every count kept under the old one, and each held finding starts again at one; a change rewrites them first. An analysis ends at the next line that opens with this word or either other marker. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-10 (asdlc-openspec-pnm); the maintainer chose a line in the analysis notes, with the loss that a hand edit breaking one resets its count unnoticed.
promptReviewRecurrenceCountMeans: How many distinct runs must have shown a finding, those in the batch and those its held lines name, before a review proposes an edit for it, unless its severity is in `promptReviewMajorSeverities`. The reviewer's session applies it before the workflow runs and holds every finding below it, and `.claude/workflows/review-prompts.js` refuses one that reaches it. It is a choice, not a measurement: a research session on 2026-09-25 found no primary source for requiring a number of occurrences before an edit (asdlc-openspec-pnm). Where it loses: a one-off minor defect that costs an hour, and recurs a week later, is paid for twice before it is fixed. 1 proposes an edit for every finding, as D-08's review did. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-10 (asdlc-openspec-pnm).
promptReviewMajorSeveritiesMeans: The severities of a finding a review proposes on one run, skipping `promptReviewRecurrenceCount`. The severities are those `.claude/agents/pr-reviewer.md` § 2. Maintainability defines, so a prompt review and the pull-request reviewer grade on one scale. Adding `minor` removes the threshold; emptying the list makes every finding wait for a second run. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-10 (asdlc-openspec-pnm).
promptReviewSkepticsMeans: How many skeptics `.claude/workflows/review-prompts.js` sends to judge one proposed edit, by its finding's severity, once the file's agent has committed it. Each reads the branch's diff and answers upheld, refuted or unverified to two questions: had the prompt said this, would the runs have gone differently; and does the edit break another path through the prompt, or another caller of it. A majority of those sent decides, and a branch merges only when every edit on it is upheld (the workflow's header holds the mechanics). The counts copy `buildReviewSkeptics`. Lowering `blocker` below 3 lets one vote decide a blocker edit or a consolidation that every later run of the prompt reads. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-10 (asdlc-openspec-pnm). A consolidation (`.claude/agents/continuous-prompt-improvement.md` § How a prompt is consolidated) goes to the `blocker` count whatever its findings' severities, because a rule it loses is lost to every later run of the prompt: added 2026-09-26 with D-12 (asdlc-openspec-aa0). `major` lowered from 3 to 1 on 2026-09-28 by D-16 (asdlc-openspec-hsg), item 3, with `buildReviewSkeptics.major`, which the maintainer chose over the recommendation to leave both for asdlc-openspec-j09.11; a batch of 5 major findings now sends 5 skeptics, where it sent 15. Where it loses: a single vote now decides a major edit that every later run of the prompt reads, the case D-10 chose three to prevent.
sessionReviewMaxFindingsMeans: The most findings the one adversarial reviewer reports in the review a session writes itself for a branch with code or a gate (`CLAUDE.md` § A workflow a session writes itself is bounded), so that it reports the ones that matter most and its skeptics stay few. A branch that changes only prompts or documents gets no such review. Decided 2026-09-28 by D-16 (asdlc-openspec-hsg), item 1, which the maintainer chose from a recommendation put with the case where it loses: a dedicated adversary that built doctored inputs found the code-fence defect in asdlc-openspec-j09.3's gate, and one general reviewer may miss that kind, which the pull-request reviewer, running nothing, will not catch.
sessionReviewSkepticsMeans: How many skeptics judge one finding of each severity in the review a session writes itself for a branch with code or a gate (`CLAUDE.md` § A workflow a session writes itself is bounded): the one skeptic's vote decides a blocker or a major finding, and a minor goes to the branch's author unjudged, as 0 says. The severities are those `.claude/agents/pr-reviewer.md` § 2. Maintainability defines. With `sessionReviewMaxFindings` findings, the review runs at most one reviewer and one skeptic for each, within `sessionWorkflowMaxAgents`. Decided 2026-09-28 by D-16 (asdlc-openspec-hsg), item 1. Where it loses: one skeptic that misreads a real major defect refutes it, where a majority of three would have outvoted it, and the branch reaches its pull request with the defect.
sessionWorkflowMaxAgentsMeans: The most agents a review or design workflow a session writes itself runs, outside `.claude/workflows/`, unless the user asks for more (`CLAUDE.md` § A workflow a session writes itself is bounded); an effort level or an orchestration default that says cost is no constraint does not raise it. Its value is the harness's workflow-size guideline that the session whose reviews led to D-16 ran under, which nothing in this repository bound (`bd show asdlc-openspec-hsg`). The review of a branch with code or a gate needs at most one reviewer and one skeptic for each of `sessionReviewMaxFindings` findings. Decided 2026-09-28 by D-16 (asdlc-openspec-hsg), item 4. Where it loses: a design question that needs more independent readings than this runs as two workflows, or waits for the user to ask for more.
prReviewIssuePatternMeans: A tracker issue id, as a regular expression without anchors: this tracker's prefix, the hash, and a child's dotted suffix (`asdlc-openspec-zgh.9`). The reviewer reads the issues a pull request carries from the ids that match it inside the parentheses at the end of the pull request's title, and nowhere else: a body names follow-ups and related issues it does not carry. A title with none cites no issue, and a person merges that pull request (`docs/decisions.md` § D-07). Change it with the tracker's prefix. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewStatusContextMeans: The commit status the reviewer sets on a pull request's head commit: pending once the session that opened the pull request, or a person, marks the head with `scripts/pr-review.mjs mark` (no job has marked one since 2026-09-28, asdlc-openspec-08a), until the reviewer has judged that commit, then success, failure or error with the reason in its description. It is what `gh pr checks --watch` waits on, so an agent watching its own pull request (`.claude/skills/open-pr/SKILL.md` § 6) reads the review's outcome as it reads any check. A verdict that needs a person sets success, not pending, so no watcher waits on a person. Renaming it strands the pending status on every open pull request until its next push. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewRequiredCheckMeans: The check run that must have passed on a commit before the reviewer acts on it: the one job of `.github/workflows/verify.yml`, whose check run carries the job's name. On a pull request's head it gates the review, so no review is spent on a head CI has refused; on `main`'s head it gates every merge, so after a bad merge the reviewer stops merging until `main` is green again. `npm run pr-review:check` refuses a `verify.yml` with no job of this name and a `pr-review.yml` whose `workflow_run` does not name that workflow. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewLabelsMeans: The labels the reviewer reads and writes on a pull request, each key its role and each value its spelling. `changes`: a dimension failed, and the author fixes the branch; the next push is reviewed again. `human`: nothing failed, and a person decides, because the risk is high, a criterion could not be verified, or the title cites no issue. `approved`: a person approves the merge of the head commit the reviewer last judged. It counts only when a person with a permission in `prReviewApproverPermissions` applied it after that verdict, and an agent never applies it (`CLAUDE.md` § Git workflow). `scripts/hooks/guard-git.mjs` refuses a session's `gh` command that applies it and reads its spelling from here, so a rename moves the guard too (`docs/decisions.md` § R-01). The reviewer creates the three if they are missing. Renaming one means renaming it on the repository in the same change, and `npm run pr-review:check` refuses a `pr-review.yml` that filters on another spelling of `approved`. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewApproverPermissionsMeans: The repository permissions, as GitHub's collaborator-permission endpoint names them, of an account whose application of the approval label counts. A bot's never does. GitHub cannot tell a person from an agent acting with that person's credentials, which is `docs/decisions.md` § R-01. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewBlockingSeveritiesMeans: The severities of a maintainability finding that fail the dimension. A `minor` finding is posted in the review and blocks nothing, so the reviewer does not hold a merge on wording. The severities themselves are defined in `.claude/agents/pr-reviewer.md` § 2. Maintainability. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewContextPathsMeans: The files held to the context-engineering rubric: what an agent reads to decide what to do, meaning the rules, the prompts, the documents, the specs and the constants they cite. Every other file is held to the product rubric. `*` matches within one directory, `**` across directories, and `**/` also matches none. A file is classed by its path at the pull request's head, and the brief names each file's class, so the reviewer does not choose. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).

prReviewHighRiskPathsMeans: The floor under the reviewer's risk judgement: a pull request that adds, changes, deletes or renames a file matching one of these globs is high risk whatever the reviewer says, and merges only on a person's approval. The reviewer can raise a pull request to high but never lower one below this floor, so no pull request can argue its way past a person into changing CI, this reviewer or the rules. Removing a line lets pull requests that change that file merge without a person, and this key is itself high risk (`prReviewHighRiskJsonKeys`). Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewHighRiskJsonKeysMeans: The second half of the floor: top-level keys of committed JSON files whose value a pull request changes (added, removed or different, compared as parsed JSON) make it high risk. A trailing `*` matches any key with that prefix. It exists because the whole file is too wide: most pull requests that add a gate add a script to `package.json`, and many change another key of this file, and neither needs a person. A dependency, an install-script permission, the engine floor, or a key the reviewer decides by does. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6). prReviewMergeMethodMeans: How the reviewer merges: the method GitHub's merge endpoint takes.
